verses.text: Follow my example, just as I follow Christ's.
I commend you, brothers and sisters, because you remember me in everything and hold firmly to the traditions I passed on to you.
But I want you to understand that Christ is the head of every man, man is the head of woman, and God is the head of Christ.
Any man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
But any woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head—it is the same as if her head were shaved.
If a woman won't cover her head, she might as well cut her hair short. But if it's shameful for her to have short hair or a shaved head, she should cover her head.
A man shouldn't cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.
Man didn't come from woman; woman came from man.
And man wasn't created for woman; woman was created for man.
That's why a woman should have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
Still, in the Lord, woman isn't independent of man, and man isn't independent of woman.
Just as woman came from man, man is also born through woman. And everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it appropriate for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Doesn't nature itself teach you that long hair is dishonorable for a man,
while long hair is a woman's glory? Her hair is given to her as a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this, we have no such practice, and neither do God's churches.
In giving this next instruction, I can't praise you, because your gatherings are doing more harm than good.
First, I hear that when you gather as a church there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
Some divisions are bound to happen, so that it becomes clear who among you is genuine.
When you come together, what you're eating isn't really the Lord's Supper.
As you eat, each person goes ahead with their own meal. One goes hungry while another gets drunk.
Don't you have homes where you can eat and drink? Or do you despise God's church and shame those who have nothing? What should I say? Should I praise you? I can't praise you for this.
I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: on the night he was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread.
After giving thanks, he broke it and said, ‘This is my body, given for you. Do this to remember me.’
In the same way, after supper he took the cup and said, ‘This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this to remember me.’
Every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you announce the Lord's death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in an unworthy way is guilty of sinning against the Lord's body and blood.
Everyone should examine themselves, and then eat the bread and drink from the cup.
Anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on themselves.
That's why many of you are weak and sick, and some have died.
If we examined ourselves, we wouldn't be judged.
But when the Lord judges us, he disciplines us so that we won't be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you gather to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, they should eat at home, so your gathering won't bring judgment. I'll deal with the other matters when I come.
